html:
From 1906 the Russian government helped millions of Russian and Ukrainian peasants move east to Siberia and the Kazakh steppe. It was part of the land reforms of Prime Minister Pyotr Stolypin.

After the revolution of 1905, Stolypin wanted to calm the crowded villages of European Russia and create a class of independent farmers. Alongside the agrarian reform, which let peasants leave the village commune, the state offered cheap tickets on the new Trans-Siberian Railway, loans and free land in Asia. Special rail cars carried whole families east. Some returned, but most stayed, and Siberia's farm output grew fast until 1914.

The land was not empty. Officials took large areas of pasture from Kazakh and Kyrgyz herders and gave it to settlers. Anger over lost land was one cause of the revolt of 1916, which ended in the flight of many Kyrgyz and Kazakhs to China.
sum: From 1906 the Russian government helped millions of Russian and Ukrainian peasants move east to Siberia and the Kazakh steppe. It was part of the land reforms of Prime Minister Pyotr Stolypin.
